sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九的隐形。

sentences.en: Most of the American West is owned by the federal government.
sentences.zh: 美国西部的大部分土地都归联邦政府所有。

sentences.en: About 85% of Nevada, 61% of Alaska, and 53% of Oregon.
sentences.zh: 内华达州约有85%，阿拉斯加州有61%，俄勒冈州有53%。

sentences.en: And there have always been questions about how this immense swath of land should be used.
sentences.zh: 关于这片广袤土地应该如何使用，一直以来都存在争议。

sentences.en: Should we allow ranchers to graze cattle?
sentences.zh: 我们应该允许牧民放牧牛群吗？

sentences.en: Or should the Western land be a place where wild animals can roam free and be protected?
sentences.zh: 还是应该把西部土地变成野生动物自由游荡和受到保护的地方？

sentences.en: Or is it land we want to reserve for recreation?
sentences.zh: 或者这是我们想要保留用于休闲娱乐的土地？

sentences.en: As you can imagine, there is no consensus on the answers to those questions.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，对于这些问题并没有共识。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of strong feelings.
And over the years, those strong feelings have sometimes bubbled up to the surface
sentences.zh: 多年来，这些强烈的情感有时会浮出水面，

sentences.en: and manifested in protests and even violence.
sentences.zh: 并通过抗议甚至暴力表现出来。

sentences.en: In 2016, a group of armed militants occupied Malheur National Wildlife Refuge in Western Oregon.
sentences.zh: 2016年，一群武装民兵占领了俄勒冈州西部的马卢尔国家野生动物庇护所。

sentences.en: They were led by a cattle rancher by the name of Ammon Bundy, the son of Cliven Bundy.
sentences.zh: 他们由一位名叫阿蒙·邦迪的养牛场主领导，他是克利文·邦迪的儿子。

sentences.en: Perhaps you heard about it, but never really understood exactly what it was all about.
sentences.zh: 也许你听说过这件事，但从未真正理解它的全貌。

sentences.en: Well, today, we bring you a story from Long Reads and Oregon Public Broadcasting reported by Leah Sattilli.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们为你带来一则由利亚·萨蒂利报道的故事，它来自《长读》与俄勒冈公共广播电台。

sentences.en: And it's the first in a series they put together that looks deeply into the fascinating
sentences.zh: 这是他们制作的一个系列节目的第一集，该系列深入探讨了迷人的细节，

sentences.en: and even sometimes wonky details of how the American West is managed,
sentences.zh: 甚至有时是美国西部管理方式中那些繁琐的细节，

sentences.en: why the Bundys are so angry about it,
sentences.zh: 为什么邦迪家族对此如此愤怒，

sentences.en: and the religious ideology that undergirds their fight against the federal government.
sentences.zh: 以及支撑他们对抗联邦政府的宗教意识形态。

sentences.en: It's an amazing series that spins a good yarn,
sentences.zh: 这是一个精彩绝伦、引人入胜的系列节目，

sentences.en: but also resonates with so many aspects of current U.S.
sentences.zh: 同时也与当前美国政治的许多方面产生共鸣。
它还涉及土地管理，这对我个人来说非常激动人心。

sentences.en: It's also about land management, which is really exciting for me personally.
This is episode one of Bundyville.
By his own account, Nevada rancher Cliven Bundy never wanted to start a war with the federal government.
sentences.zh: 据内华达州牧民克利文·邦迪自己所说，他从未想过要与联邦政府开战。

sentences.en: He says that if they'd just left him alone out here in the desert,
sentences.zh: 他说，如果他们只是把他独自留在这里的沙漠中，

sentences.en: none of this would have ever started.
sentences.zh: 这一切就永远不会发生了。

sentences.en: And if you want to see him as the folksy hero of a modern-day Western,
sentences.zh: 如果你想把他当作现代西部片中具有民俗色彩的英雄，

sentences.en: you can choose to see him that way.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择这样看待他。
这是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: and it shows a blonde-haired little boy, a toddler.
sentences.zh: 画面显示了一个金发小男孩，一个蹒跚学步的幼儿。

sentences.en: He's wearing a dusty red polo shirt, blue jeans.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件沾满灰尘的红色Polo衫和蓝色牛仔裤。

sentences.en: He lays stunned in the dirt, having just been knocked down.
sentences.zh: 他刚被撞倒，惊恐地躺在泥土里。

sentences.en: And he's considering whether or not he wants to cry.
sentences.zh: 他正在考虑自己到底要不要哭。
爷爷能帮把你扶起来吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I hope that leg's not broke.
The boy shakes off his cowboy hat wearing Grandpa and putters away.
sentences.zh: 小男孩甩开戴着牛仔帽的爷爷，慢吞吞地走开了。

sentences.en: That's what life's all about, raising cowboys.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活的全部意义，培养牛仔。

sentences.en: He got run over by a horse, and he's out there going already.
sentences.zh: 他被马轧了过去，现在已经活蹦乱跳地出去了。

sentences.en: The toddler looks back at his Grandpa.
sentences.zh: 幼儿回头看了看他的爷爷。

sentences.en: He points to the west, and the camera follows.
sentences.zh: 他指向西方，镜头随之移动。

sentences.en: A patch of bright green grass comes into view against the Nevada desert.
sentences.zh: 在内华达沙漠的衬托下，一小片翠绿的草地进入了视野。

sentences.en: It's the color of life, and it stands out in a place where everything else looks dead.
sentences.zh: 那是生命的的颜色，在一个万物看起来都死气沉沉的地方格外醒目。
这片土地是我们的土地。

sentences.en: This land is a free land.
sentences.zh: 这片土地是自由的土地。

sentences.en: This land is a place that we can enjoy and use.
sentences.zh: 这片土地是我们能够享受和使用的土地。

sentences.en: That's Cliven Bundy as he'd like to be seen.
sentences.zh: 这就是克利文·邦迪希望被人们看到的样子。

sentences.en: The peaceful farmer, homesteading on his 160-acre ranch near Bunkerville, Nevada.
sentences.zh: 这个爱好和平的农夫，在内华达州邦克维尔附近的160英亩牧场上开垦家园。

sentences.en: But in 2014, just a few weeks after this video was shot, on the same piece of land, Cliven Bundy and his sons were anything but peaceful.
sentences.zh: 但在2014年，就在这段视频拍摄几周后，在同一块土地上，克利文·邦迪和他的儿子们一点也不和平。

sentences.en: They'd raised a militia that was pointing guns at federal agents of what the Bundys called a tyrannical government.
sentences.zh: 他们组建了一支民兵队伍，将枪口对准了联邦特工，邦迪家族称之为暴政政府。

sentences.en: Here he is on stage in Bunkerville, whipping the crowd into a frenzy,
sentences.zh: 他在邦克维尔的舞台上，煽动着人群的情绪，

sentences.en: demanding that the local sheriff bulldoze the buildings at a nearby national park
sentences.zh: 要求当地治安官推倒附近国家公园的建筑，

sentences.en: so that the surrounding community might have free reign of the land.
sentences.zh: 以便周围的社区能够对这片土地拥有绝对的控制权。

sentences.en: You take them, but you get the county.
sentences.zh: 你们占领它们，但你们要控制县里。

sentences.en: He says, get the county equipment out there and tear those things down this morning.
sentences.zh: 他说，今天早上就把县里的设备弄到那里去，把那些东西拆掉。

sentences.en: The sheriff just stands quietly on stage.
sentences.zh: 治安官只是静静地站在台上。

sentences.en: He's got his thumbs hitched in his belt, and the mob heckles him.
sentences.zh: 他的大拇指勾在皮带里，暴民们对发出嘘声起哄。

sentences.en: We want those arms to live.
sentences.zh: 我们希望那些武器能够生存。

sentences.en: He says the sheriff also has to disarm the Park Service Rangers.
sentences.zh: 他说治安官还必须解除公园管理局护林员的武装。

sentences.en: Bring me those guns in one hour, he says, or else.
sentences.zh: 把那些枪在一个小时内交给我，他说，否则后果自负。

sentences.en: If they're not done, then we'll decide what we're going to do from this point on.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不这样做，那我们将决定从这一点开始要做什么。

sentences.en: Depending on how you look at the way this is all played out,
sentences.zh: 取决于你如何看待这一切的发展，

sentences.en: Cliven Bundy is either a prophet who's leading his people to salvation,
sentences.zh: 克利文·邦迪要么是引领他的子民走向救赎的先知，

sentences.en: or a cult leader who's led his followers straight to jail, even death.
sentences.zh: 要么是把追随者直接带进监狱甚至死亡的邪教头目。

sentences.en: And how you see Cliven may say just as much about you as it does about the Bundys.
sentences.zh: 你如何看待克利文，可能不仅反映了你，也反映了邦迪家族。

sentences.en: From Longreads and Oregon Public Broadcasting, this is Bundyville.
sentences.zh: 来自长读与俄勒冈公共广播电台，这里是《邦迪镇》。

sentences.en: A seven-part series about the Bundy family and how they're changing the American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于邦迪家族以及他们如何改变美国西部的七集系列节目。

sentences.en: I'm Leah Satili, and in 2016, I set out to write a single breaking news story about the Bundys.
sentences.zh: 我是利亚·萨蒂利，在2016年，我着手撰写一篇关于邦迪家族的突发新闻报道。

sentences.en: But one story turned into several.
sentences.zh: 但一个故事演变成了好几个故事。

sentences.en: Because every time I learned something new, it would just bring up more questions.
sentences.zh: 因为每次我了解到新东西，就会引发更多的问题。

sentences.en: Things that seemed unbelievable would turn out to be real.
sentences.zh: 看起来令人难以置信的事情最后都被证明是真的。

sentences.en: Even when I wasn't writing, I couldn't stop finding new pieces in this really complicated puzzle.
sentences.zh: 即使在我没有写作的时候，我也无法停止在这个非常复杂的拼图中寻找新的碎片。

sentences.en: Most people know roughly what happened in Nevada and Oregon.
sentences.zh: 大多数人大概知道内华达州和俄勒冈州发生了什么。

sentences.en: If not, this first episode is going to bring you up to speed.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，第一集将带你了解最新情况。

sentences.en: And then we're going to dive into all the weird stuff that didn't make it on the nightly news.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将深入探讨所有没有登上晚间新闻的诡异事情。

sentences.en: And the things that have only come to light months and years after most people stopped paying attention.
sentences.zh: 以及在大多数人停止关注几个月甚至几年后才浮出水面的事情。

sentences.en: Because the Bundys story is bigger and stranger than I expected.
sentences.zh: 因为邦迪家族的故事比我预期的还要庞大和诡异。

sentences.en: More than anything else, the story of the Bundys is about belief and truth.
sentences.zh: 与其他任何事情相比，邦迪家族的故事关乎信仰和真相。

sentences.en: And figuring out which one of those things has more power.
sentences.zh: 并弄清楚这两者中哪一个拥有更大的力量。

sentences.en: If you believe the Bundys, then you believe the federal government is trying to enslave the American people.
sentences.zh: 如果你相信邦迪家族，那么你就相信联邦政府正试图奴役美国人民。

sentences.en: If you believe the feds, then you believe a remote cattle rancher is a domestic terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你相信联邦调查局，那么你就相信一个偏远的牧场主是个本土恐怖分子。

sentences.en: So, do the Bundys own the truth?
sentences.zh: 那么，邦迪家族拥有真相吗？

sentences.en: Or is that the property of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 还是那是美国政府的财产？

sentences.en: That's what I set out to find.
sentences.zh: 这就是我出发去寻找的答案。

sentences.en: Let's think for a second about all the things in history that have started armed revolts against a government.
sentences.zh: 让我们花一秒钟想想历史上所有引发针对政府武装起义的事情。

sentences.en: Where do reptiles fit on that list?
sentences.zh: 爬行动物在那份名单上排在什么位置？

sentences.en: For Cliven, right at the top.
sentences.zh: 对克利文来说，排在最前面。

sentences.en: Here's Aaron Weiss from the Conservation Advocacy Group, the Center for Western Priorities.
sentences.zh: 这是来自保护倡导组织“西部优先中心”的亚伦·韦斯。

sentences.en: You know, the whole reason that Cliven Bundy has been breaking the law and running his cows illegally
sentences.zh: 你知道，克利文·邦迪一直违法并违规放牧牛群的全部原因，

sentences.en: is because his cows posed a danger to the desert tortoise.
sentences.zh: 是因为他的牛对沙漠陆龟构成了危险。

sentences.en: It was an endangered species problem to begin with.
sentences.zh: 最初这是一个濒危物种问题。

sentences.en: In the early 1990s, populations of desert tortoise were plummeting in the American SouthweSt.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代初，美国西南部的沙漠陆龟种群数量正在急剧下降。

sentences.en: The tortoises have been around for 15 to 20 million years in the desert.
sentences.zh: 陆龟已经在沙漠中存在了1500万到2000万年。

sentences.en: But they compete with cattle for what little grass there is to eat out there.
sentences.zh: 但它们为了争夺外面那点可怜的草来吃，要与牛竞争。

sentences.en: In the 90s, that landed the tortoise on the endangered species liSt.
sentences.zh: 在90年代，这使得陆龟被列入了濒危物种名单。

sentences.en: It's a common story in the WeSt.
An endangered species is threatened by ranching or logging or mining.
sentences.zh: 濒危物种受到牧业、伐木或采矿的威胁。

sentences.en: Regulators and environmentalists step in to preserve the animal.
sentences.zh: 监管机构和环保主义者介入保护动物。

sentences.en: The groups go to court and fight over this one central question.
sentences.zh: 各方诉诸法庭，并围绕这个核心问题展开斗争。

sentences.en: Are the wide-open spaces in the West meant to support rural communities?
sentences.zh: 西部广阔无垠的空间是为了支持农村社区吗？

sentences.en: Or should they be kept pristine?
Historically, the people working the land have had to back off, give up resources and old ways of life,
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，在土地上劳作的人们不得不退让，放弃资源和旧的生活方式，

sentences.en: But at a certain point, the Bundys decided they just weren't going to change.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，邦迪家族决定他们就是不打算改变。

sentences.en: They were done with federal rules.
We run cattle here, graze this natural resource off this public land,
sentences.zh: 我们在这里放牧牛群，在这片公共土地上吃掉这些自然资源，

sentences.en: and I abide by all of Nevada state law.
sentences.zh: 我遵守内华达州的所有法律。

sentences.en: But I don't recognize the United States government as even existing.
sentences.zh: 但我甚至不承认美国政府的存在。

sentences.en: Since 1948, the Bundys have been growing melons and raising cattle on their 160 acres.
sentences.zh: 自1948年以来，邦迪家族一直在他们的160英亩土地上种植甜瓜和养牛。

sentences.en: And for decades, the family also paid the federal government for a grazing permit
sentences.zh: 几十年来，该家族还向联邦政府支付放牧许可证费用，

sentences.en: so they could legally ranch on the public land that surrounds the property.
sentences.zh: 以便他们能够在环绕该物业的公共土地上合法放牧。

sentences.en: For Nevada ranchers, the tortoise listing meant three fewer months each year
sentences.zh: 对于内华达州的牧民来说，陆龟被列入名单意味着每年少放牧三个月，

sentences.en: that they could graze their herds.
In 1993, he started simply ignoring the ruling and kept his cows on the land.
sentences.zh: 1993年，他开始简单地忽视这项裁决，并把他的牛留在了这片土地上。

sentences.en: You should know that the rates ranchers pay for grazing are like a dollar per cow each year.
sentences.zh: 你应该知道，牧民支付的放牧费用就像每年每头牛一美元左右。

sentences.en: Ranchers buy the permits because land is expensive,
sentences.zh: 牧民购买许可证是因为土地昂贵，

sentences.en: and the majority of land in the West is actually federally owned.
sentences.zh: 而且西部的大部分土地实际上都属于联邦所有。

sentences.en: But Aaron Weiss says that's one of the things that's up for debate in the eyes of the Bundys.
sentences.zh: 但亚伦·韦斯说，在邦迪家族看来，这是争论的焦点之一。

sentences.en: Whether or not grazing your cattle on a piece of public land gives you any rights to that property.
sentences.zh: 在公共土地上一块土地上放牧牛是否赋予你对该财产的任何权利。

sentences.en: Cliven Bundy believes he is grazing his cows on his land,
sentences.zh: 克利文·邦迪认为他是在自己的土地上放牧牛群，

sentences.en: and he's going to claim it's not federal government land, it's actually county land, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 他要声称这不是联邦政府的土地，实际上是县里的土地，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Ranchers in Clark County, Nevada, were eventually offered buyouts for their grazing permits
sentences.zh: 内华达州克拉克县的牧民最终获得了放牧许可证的买断补偿，

sentences.en: to help save the desert tortoise.
Nearly all of them took the money, and their permits were retired.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都拿了钱，他们的许可证被收回了。
除了克利文·邦迪，每个人都拿了。

sentences.en: For more than 20 years, Bundy fought in and out of court with the Federal Bureau of Land Management.
sentences.zh: 20多年来，邦迪一直在联邦土地管理局的法庭内外部进行斗争。

sentences.en: You'll hear about the BLM a lot in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你在这个播客中会经常听到关于BLM的事情。

sentences.en: It's the agency that President Truman created after World War II
sentences.zh: 这是杜鲁门总统在二战后创建的机构，

sentences.en: to manage millions of acres owned by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 旨在管理美国政府拥有的数百万英亩土地，
其中大部分在西部各州。

sentences.en: most of it in western states.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分在西部各州。

sentences.en: But Bundy said that was unconstitutional.
If you're around the Bundys and their supporters for any amount of time,
sentences.zh: 如果你和邦迪家族及其支持者在一起呆上一段时间，

sentences.en: they'll hand you a pocket-sized copy of the Constitution,
sentences.zh: 他们会递给你一本袖珍版的宪法，

sentences.en: and they'll tell you about their favorite part.
sentences.zh: 并会告诉你他们最喜欢的部分。
宪法第一条第八款第十七项。

sentences.en: All right, let me read that clause to you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我把那款读给你们听。

sentences.en: Again, this is Article 1, Section 8, Clause 17.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是宪法第一条第八款第十七项。

sentences.en: Now, it starts out that says Congress shall have power to...
sentences.zh: 好，它一开始说国会有权……

sentences.en: Legal scholars call it the Enclave Clause,
sentences.zh: 法律学者称之为“领地条款”，

sentences.en: and it basically says the government needs to get state permission
sentences.zh: 它的大意是政府需要获得州的许可

sentences.en: to use land outside of Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 才能使用华盛顿特区以外的土地。

sentences.en: The Bundys claim even when they have that permission,
sentences.zh: 邦迪家族声称，即便他们获得了这种许可，

sentences.en: the feds can only build things like forts and military dockyards.
sentences.zh: 联邦也只能建造堡垒和军事船坞之类的东西。

sentences.en: is that it completely ignores the rest of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它完全忽视了宪法的其余部分。

sentences.en: There are other clauses in long-settled Supreme Court cases
sentences.zh: 还有其他条款以及早已定论的最高法院判例

sentences.en: that say the government definitely can own land.
sentences.zh: 表明政府绝对可以拥有土地。
我们稍后会深入探讨这一点，

sentences.en: but it's also important to know
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是要知道，

sentences.en: that the other ingredient here is sovereign citizen ideology.
sentences.zh: 这里的另一个成份是“主权公民”意识形态。

sentences.en: they are independent nations unto themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己就是独立的国家。

sentences.en: And when you're your own nation,
sentences.zh: 而当你是自己的国家时，

sentences.en: you don't have to abide by the country's laws.
sentences.zh: 你就不必遵守国家的法律。
联邦法官不是真正的法官。
